name: King
description: King is a compendium card game played in many countries including Belgium, Italy, Portugal, Russia, Turkey, Colombia, and Brazil. Despite its English name, there is no evidence it was ever played in English-speaking countries. The game consists of a series of rounds with different objectivesâ€”some negative (avoiding specific cards or tricks) and some positive (winning tricks). It is closely related to Barbu, Kierki, and Trex.
origin: Unknown; Russian version dates to 1920s. Popular in Belgium, Portugal, Russia, Turkey, Colombia, Brazil, Italy.

history.origins: The game is known by the English name 'King' in many non-English speaking countries, leading to speculation about English origins. However, no evidence exists of it being played in English-speaking countries. It likely evolved from European compendium games in the early 20th century.

setup.players: 4 players playing individually (partnerships form in some variants).
setup.deck: Standard 52-card deck. Aces are generally high.
setup.dealing: Each player receives 13 cards. The dealer rotates clockwise.

rules.objective: Complete a series of rounds with different objectives. Accumulate the highest score (or lowest penalty) after all rounds.
rules.gameplay:
1. Standard trick-taking rules apply: must follow suit if possible
2. In negative rounds, players try to avoid taking penalty cards or tricks
3. In positive rounds, players try to win tricks
4. Scoring varies by regional variant
keyRules: Must follow suit if able; otherwise any card.
In No Hearts and No King of Hearts, hearts may not be led unless no choice; King of Hearts must be played if unable to follow suit.
Negative rounds: avoid tricks, hearts, men (K/J), queens, last two tricks, or King of Hearts per contract.
Positive rounds: win tricks or target cards for plus points.
Two rounds of six contracts (12 games); lowest total penalty or highest total score wins.

strategy.basic: In negative rounds, try to void yourself in the penalty suit early so you can discard penalty cards on tricks won by others. Save low cards for when you must win tricks.
strategy.intermediate: Track which penalty cards have been played. In the King of Hearts round, if you hold the King, try to void a suit to dump it safely. Count cards to know when penalty cards might appear.
strategy.advanced: In positive rounds, coordinate with implied partners to maximize tricks. In negative rounds, force opponents to take tricks by leading suits where they have high cards. Manage your hand across all rounds, saving certain cards for specific upcoming rounds.
tips: Always keep track of the King of Hearts in the corresponding roundâ€”it is the most damaging single card
In No Queens rounds, remember there are four Queens to avoid
In Trump rounds, the dealer's choice of trump reveals information about their hand
Balance your play: doing well in negative rounds is as important as positive rounds
